MEET THE HIRING MANAGER

Hi, I'm Kim Beaudin, Development Manager at Jane. For the last year I've been responsible for building the engineering side of Jane's marketing platform from the ground up. Now we're building something new: a small, founding engineering team responsible for Jane's customer data infrastructure.

Jane is used by thousands of clinics and hundreds of thousands of practitioners every day — and we're growing. As we scale, the decisions we're making are getting more complex and higher stakes. Those decisions deserve a data foundation that's built for where we're headed, not just where we've been. We've done a lot with what we have. Smart people across engineering, BI, and marketing have built real value, but we've reached a point where event instrumentation, attribution, and identity resolution need dedicated ownership to take the next step.

This is a new, founding team within our Engineering org. The infrastructure that powers Jane's customer decisions exists today, but it's been built incrementally, across teams, without dedicated ownership. Together, you'll assess what we have, help define where we're headed, and build the systems and standards that get us there. Some of what exists will stay. Some will be replaced. All of it needs a cohesive strategy.

The team owns the collection and delivery layer end-to-end, event pipelines, CDP tooling, and source integrations. Our scope covers schema governance, source management, instrumentation standards and infrastructure, identity resolution, attribution capture, and a lightweight review process before new events ship. You'll help set architectural direction, evaluate current tooling, define our data collection strategy, and build the systems that make it real.

If you've ever wanted to own the engineering foundation that an entire company's customer data insights runs on: assessing what exists, deciding what stays and what goes, and building the event pipelines, schemas, and identity resolution layer from the ground up. This is that opportunity.



WHAT IMPACT WE'RE LOOKING FOR YOU TO MAKE

 - Own the how, not just the what: apply strong product sense to set direction, shape standards, and elevate execution.

 - Build and maintain Jane's customer data infrastructure end-to-end: the systems, pipelines, and source integrations that carry product and marketing events from collection to warehouse. Today there are multiple independently configured sources with different conventions; you'll bring consistency and reliability.

 - Work directly with marketing, paid media, analytics, marketing operations, BI, and product as primary stakeholders, including on attribution questions, campaign tracking, conversion data, and the integrations that connect our marketing tools to the warehouse. The stakeholder surface is wide and cross-functional, and your ability to build trust across teams matters as much as your technical depth.

 - Drive tooling strategy for Jane's collection layer, including our CDP, event pipeline, and ingestion infrastructure. We currently run RudderStack and are evaluating the right long-term stack; you'll help determine what that looks like and build toward it while keeping the lights on.

 - Establish instrumentation standards within engineering, product, and marketing, defining how product and web events are structured, named, versioned, and validated, while ensuring clean handoffs, shared standards, and alignment on what good data looks like at Jane.

 - Take ownership of identity resolution and attribution at the collection layer. A prospect's journey crosses multiple channels, domains, and touchpoints (including marketing pages, landing pages on third-party platforms, and a separate signup application), and that journey needs to stitch together cleanly so that funnel data is trustworthy and Jane has a reliable picture of what's driving growth.

 - Navigate the realities of consent-gated instrumentation. Jane operates in healthcare, which means our tracking infrastructure interacts with PHI compliance requirements, consent management, tag management, and third-party marketing tools. You'll design instrumentation that works reliably within those constraints.


WHAT EXPERIENCE WE NEED

 - A University Degree in Computer Science or a related STEM field plus hands-on experience as a data engineer or similar, including time operating at a staff level or higher — depth and judgment matter more here than a specific number of years. You've built and maintained event collection, customer data infrastructure, or data pipeline systems in production. You've inherited and rationalized independently built pipelines, not just built from scratch.

 - You're comfortable leading and owning both the strategy as well as the execution: making the architectural calls, being the person other teams and leadership look to for direction on this domain, set standards that teams actually follow. You influence and drive strategy clearly across engineering, product, BI, marketing, and leadership.

 - Experience evaluating or implementing Customer Data Platforms including migrating or consolidating existing tooling. Greenfield-only experience is not sufficient for this role.

 - Experience with privacy-compliant tracking and consent management. You've worked with consent management platforms, understand how consent state affects data collection, and have designed instrumentation that holds up within those constraints, ideally including server-side tagging or tag management systems. Experience in healthcare or other regulated environments is a plus.

 - Strong opinions (loosely held) on schema design, event taxonomy, and data quality. You've seen what happens when instrumentation is an afterthought, and you care about getting it right.

 - Experience with identity resolution, attribution, or cross-domain tracking. You understand the complexities of stitching a user journey across systems and have ideas about how to make it less hard.

 - Proficiency in JavaScript or TypeScript and SQL (required). Python is a strong asset. Familiarity with Snowflake, Looker, or similar warehouse and BI tooling is helpful; you won't own that layer, but you'll need a shared vocabulary with the teams that do.

 - Comfort working with AI tools as part of your day-to-day workflow. We're a team that embraces AI to work smarter, and we expect the same from the people we hire.

If you don’t meet every single qualification but are excited about this role, we’d still love to hear from you.




MORE ABOUT JANE

Jane is a founder-led, high-growth SaaS company with a remote-first team working across Canada, the US, and the UK, united by our mission to help the helpers.

We build the products and tools that thousands of clinics rely on every day to run their businesses, care for their patients, and grow their communities. That level of impact means every person at Jane plays an important role in how we show up for our customers. We're all responsible for being deeply connected to their needs, obsessed with improving their experience, and proud of the difference our work makes in their day-to-day lives.

Jane is growing fast, and that growth brings exciting challenges that call for adaptability, resilience, learning agility, and humility. We're proud of what we've built and quick to admit what we don't know yet. We listen, learn, and adjust as we go. More than 70,000 businesses run on Jane which has 250,000+ practitioners interacting with our product on a daily basis and growth is continuing to accelerate.

Our goal isn't just delivery - it's delight. We move quickly, communicate openly, and solve real problems together. If you're energized by ambiguity, motivated by impact, and eager to learn with others, you'll thrive at Jane.




COMPENSATION & BENEFITS

At Jane, we’re committed to paying fairly, clearly, and above all, paying for growth. You'll see that our salary ranges are quite large - this is intentional. It reflects the full growth journey someone might take in the role, from developing skills early on to becoming highly proficient and ultimately achieving excellence. Most new hires join at the accomplished stage. A starting salary below this typically indicates a candidate with strong potential who is still developing key skills. Salaries above this usually apply to existing team members who have made a significant impact and bring deep Jane-specific knowledge.

 - 🇺🇸 For candidates based in the United States, the annual salary range is $149,600 - $233,800, with the accomplished stage at $177,000 USD.

 - 🇨🇦 For candidates based in Canada, the annual salary range is $152,000 – $237,500 CAD, with the accomplished stage at $180,500 CAD.

We believe in paying for growth. You’ll have regular career development conversations with your manager and your compensation will grow as you gain experience and contribute meaningfully to our mission.

Paying clearly is one of our compensation fundamentals. Watch this https://vimeo.com/880258361 short video to learn how our salary bands are set. You’re also encouraged to ask questions about compensation at any point during the interview process.

We also offer a comprehensive benefits package, You can learn more about it here https://jane.app/documents/hiring/jane_benefits_overview.pdf!


Jane takes job scams and candidate fraud seriously. Jane will only contact you from an @jane.app http://jane.app email address. We'll never contact you from a personal email, ask for payment, or request purchases during the hiring process. If something doesn't seem right, please reach out to us at hiring@jane.app before sharing any personal information.

ABOUT THE ROLE

Hi, I'm Scott, and I lead the Cloud Engineering team at Jane. I've spent a couple of decades keeping large platforms running and scaling at companies like Loblaw and Achievers, and I joined Jane to help our platform meet its next stage of growth.

Cloud Engineering owns the infrastructure that underpins the whole Jane platform. We keep it running, monitor it, scale it, and add capacity as our clinics grow. We're also the team people come to when they aren't sure where a problem belongs, so we end up working across almost every part of engineering.

Our platform has served Jane well for more than a decade, and we're now approaching an inflection point. A big part of this role is figuring out what it takes to scale it cleanly for the company's next stage of growth.

You'll work alongside other Staff engineers in our team to help shape the long-term vision for our infrastructure alongside our staff and senior staff engineers, then break that vision into pieces we can start delivering now.

Just as important as the technical work is how you show up. The team needs a driver: someone who runs at hard, ambiguous problems, is often first to jump in and help, and can bring several teams together to build consensus to land big ideas. We can't scale Jane on our own, so building partnerships and championing change is core to the job.

You'll work with a modern, cloud-native stack at real scale, with plenty of room to raise the bar for how we use our tools, including AI. If you like solving gnarly infrastructure problems and making everyone around you more effective, I'd love to meet you.



WHAT IMPACT WE'RE LOOKING FOR YOU TO MAKE

 - Help set the longer-term technical vision for Jane's infrastructure alongside our staff and senior staff engineers, then turn that vision into concrete pieces the team can deliver along the way.

 - Act as a driver on hard, ambiguous problems, looking past the symptom to the real issue and seeing it through to resolution even when it spans several teams.

 - Champion change across engineering by building the relationships and consensus needed to land big infrastructure improvements, since scaling Jane is never a solo effort.

 - Provide technical leadership to other teams, helping them design cloud infrastructure for new features and make sound architectural choices.

 - Improve day-to-day operational health by reducing noisy alerts, hardening the platform, and making the whole system easier to run.

 - Work closely with our Application Security Team to harden our infrastructure against security and compliance requirements.

 - Bring an AI-positive mindset, helping the team get more leverage from AI tooling while respecting that infrastructure changes carry a real blast radius.


WHAT EXPERIENCE WE NEED

 - Deep expertise with AWS, including multi-region deployments and high-scale, highly available cloud services.

 - Strong command of infrastructure as code, particularly Terraform.

 - Solid infrastructure architecture skills, with a clear sense of how to assemble AWS building blocks into scalable, reliable systems.

 - Experience operating databases at scale. Including upgrades, scaling, performance tuning and capacity planning.

 - A track record of running large projects and driving consensus across many stakeholders. For this role, that attitude and problem-solving ability matter to us as much as raw technical depth. Can you look past a symptom to find the real problem, then work across several teams to get it solved?

 - Experience operating at a company of meaningful scale that's growing quickly, ideally with a "been there, done that" perspective on scaling infrastructure through rapid growth. You're comfortable somewhere between a small startup and a large enterprise, in that fast-growth middle.

 - An AI-positive mindset and hands-on experience using AI as a coding and research tool, with the judgment to know when to direct it and when to step in. At the staff level, we expect you to guide these tools well and explain the decisions behind your work.

 - Comfort participating in an on-call rotation.

 - Staff engineers here act as technical leaders, so we're looking for someone who sets direction, raises the bar, and lifts up the people around them..

Hi, I'm Shane, and I lead the Patient Booking Web team at Jane. I started out writing software for medical devices and for oceanographers. Over the last decade or so I've led development teams at places like Amazon, Hootsuite, and Coinbase. What I care about most is building software that real people rely on, inside a team where everyone gets to grow.

Patient Booking Web is a newer team with a very public-facing job. We own the places patients go on the web to connect with their clinic: the online booking page, My Account, and the booking experience clinics embed on their own websites. Every time a patient books a physio session, a massage, or a counselling appointment online, they're using something we built. Making that moment simple and welcoming is one of the most direct ways we get to help the helpers.

The work ahead is big. We're modernizing patient booking and moving it to React one piece at a time, and it stays live the whole way for every clinic and patient who depends on it. Along the way we want booking to be truly accessible, so patients using a keyboard or a screen reader can book as easily as anyone else. We also want booking to work well on a phone and to be easy for clinics to embed wherever their patients are. We have plans and architecture ideas we're excited about, and we'd love someone to pressure test them and look around the corners we haven't checked yet.

That's where you come in. As our Staff Developer, you'll be the technical leader on a small, curious team. You'll help shape the architecture, write code alongside us, and mentor developers who are earlier in their careers and eager to grow. If turning a long-lived product into something patients love sounds like fun to you, I'd really like to meet you.



THE IMPACT YOU COULD HAVE

 - Help shape the architecture for moving Online Booking and My Account to React, including routing, data, state, and how legacy and new code share a page while we migrate one section at a time.

 - Strengthen the team's existing plans by spotting risks early and bringing clear options to the table, so we land on decisions everyone can stand behind.

 - Write code every week across React, TypeScript, and Rails, setting the patterns the rest of the team will build on.

 - Champion accessibility from the very first commit, so keyboard behaviour, focus management, and screen reader support are built in from the start and backed by testing that shows they work.

 - Grow the developers around you through mentorship, pairing, and code reviews that help people learn and build confidence.

 - Partner with Design on our component library to close the gaps the booking experience needs.

 - Work with the teams whose pages live inside the booking flow, so they can move to React on their own timelines.

 - Drive safe, gradual rollouts with feature flags and production monitoring, so big changes ship in small steps that can be paused at any time.

 - Bring a pragmatic, responsible approach to AI, using agentic workflows to speed up the migration where they genuinely help while keeping a thoughtful human eye on quality.



THE EXPERIENCE WE FEEL WE NEED

 - Around 10 or more years of building software professionally, with experience working at a staff or technical lead level.

 - Deep, hands-on expertise in React and TypeScript, including client-side routing, browser history, and state management with Redux Toolkit or something similar.

 - A full stack background with real frontend strength, ideally including moving a legacy frontend to React in stages while it stayed live in production.

 - Practical experience applying WCAG 2.1 AA to real interfaces, including keyboard behaviour, focus management, and ARIA.

 - Comfort designing APIs alongside backend colleagues, plus experience with feature flags, gradual rollouts, and production monitoring.

 - A track record of technical leadership, where you've written design docs, made thoughtful calls in uncertain moments, and helped other developers grow.

 - A collaborative, low-ego style where you write down your reasoning, change your mind when the evidence says to, and raise concerns early and kindly with options in hand.

 - Everyday use of AI in your coding workflow, and curiosity about using it systematically, through things like agentic workflows, to move large migrations forward.

 - Experience with Ruby on Rails is a nice-to-have that will help you ramp up quickly, and we're happy to support you in learning it on the job.

 - Bonus points for hands-on screen reader testing with tools like JAWS or NVDA, or for building embeddable widgets or web components that run on other people's websites.

ABOUT THE ROLE

We're rebuilding how we manage data and analytics at Jane. Our goal is to establish a trusted data foundation that powers self-service analytics, AI, and consistent business metrics across the company.

This role is focused on Product Analytics—but not in the traditional sense of generating insights or building dashboards. Instead, you'll focus on building the technical foundation that enables Product teams to answer their own questions with confidence.

You'll partner closely with Engineering, Product, and Growth to improve product instrumentation, build scalable dbt models, standardize business logic, and create governed datasets that power reporting, experimentation, and AI. You'll also help establish the standards for how product data is modeled, tested, documented, and maintained as our analytics platform continues to evolve.

If you enjoy solving complex technical problems, building scalable data foundations, and enabling others through trusted data, this role is a great fit.




WHAT IMPACT WE’RE LOOKING FOR YOU TO MAKE

 - Build and maintain the product analytics data foundation that powers reporting, self-service, experimentation, and AI.

 - Partner with Engineering to define, implement, and validate product instrumentation before new features are released.

 - Design and maintain scalable dbt models that transform raw product events into trusted analytical datasets.

 - Build semantic models, standardized business logic, and governed metric definitions that ensure consistent product metrics across dashboards, self-service, and AI.

 - Develop certified datasets that power modern analytics and visualization platforms such as Looker, Omni, Hex, and similar technologies.

 - Partner with Product Managers to translate business requirements into scalable, trusted, and reusable analytical data models.

 - Monitor product data pipelines, identify instrumentation gaps and data quality issues, and implement scalable, long-term improvements.

 - Continuously improve how product data is modeled, governed, documented, and consumed across the analytics platform.

 - Leverage AI to accelerate analytics engineering workflows, including data modeling, testing, documentation, and code development.


WHAT EXPERIENCE WE NEED

 - 6+ years of experience in Product Data Analyst, Analytics Engineering, or a similarly technical data role within a SaaS or high-growth technology company.

 - Expert-level SQL skills and deep experience designing scalable analytical data models, with a strong understanding of data architecture and query performance optimization.

 - 6+ years of experience building, deploying, and maintaining dbt projects in production environments.

 - Experience modeling behavioral product data and building event-driven analytical datasets.

 - Experience partnering with Engineering teams to define product instrumentation requirements and improve the quality and reliability of product event data.

 - Experience working with Customer Data Platforms (CDPs) such as Segment or RudderStack.

 - Experience designing semantic models, reusable business logic, governed datasets, and trusted metric definitions that enable consistent analytics across multiple consumption layers.

 - Experience implementing data quality testing, documentation, observability, and governance best practices.

 - Experience building or supporting modern analytics and visualization platforms such as Looker, Omni, Hex, Sigma, or similar technologies.

 - Strong understanding of how semantic models and governed metrics are consumed across dashboards, self-service analytics, and AI experiences.

 - Experience working with modern cloud data platforms such as Snowflake, BigQuery, or Redshift.

 - Experience using AI tools such as Cursor, Claude Code, or similar technologies to improve analytics engineering workflows.

 - Strong communication skills and the ability to partner effectively with Engineering, Product, Analytics, and business stakeholders.

ABOUT THE ROLE

Hi, I'm Megan https://www.linkedin.com/in/meganstewart99/, and I lead the Product Security team at Jane. Product Security work day to day with the developers building the software that 70,000+ clinics use to book, chart, and bill. My view of security is that it's a partnership with developers. The people who do well here can take complex insights and make them digestible for a busy team, and focus on fixing the cause, rather than repeatedly fixing the effects of an issue.

We need a staff-level engineer who can identify the themes that tie together the insights we uncover and work with product teams to better how we build secure software at the architecture level. There's a full roadmap behind that too: changes to how our development lifecycle and GitHub workflows run, private package repositories, maturing our SCA tooling, and a security champions program. You'd lead some of those projects outright.

We also lean into AI on this team, in the back office and in the product. We're already automating reporting and reminders, and the next step is using AI for vulnerability analysis and getting closer to the code with draft fixes. If you've been somewhere that kept AI locked away and you want to build with it, or you're already securing AI features and want to do it at scale, this is a great place for that.




WHAT IMPACT WE'RE LOOKING FOR YOU TO MAKE

 - Turn recurring AppSec findings into architectural fixes by spotting the common themes across vulnerabilities and partnering with product teams to design them out, rather than patching one instance at a time.

 - Lead product security projects end to end, starting with private package repositories, maturing our SCA tooling, and the changes to how our development lifecycle and GitHub workflows run.

 - Build AI into how the team works, moving us from automated reminders and reporting to AI-assisted vulnerability analysis and draft fixes that land closer to the code. (unconfirmed pending recruiter follow-up)

 - Champion secure development across Jane by building trusted relationships with developers, explaining risk in plain language, and helping long-tenured teams adopt new practices without friction.

 - Own security initiatives and represent Product Security in cross-functional groups, and mentor teammates as the team's most senior hands-on engineer.


WHAT EXPERIENCE WE NEED

 - Staff-level application security experience, including owning security initiatives end to end and working directly with development teams.

 - A real development background. Ruby on Rails is ideal; Python, Java, or C# with a willingness to get into a Rails codebase works too. You can read a draft PR and tell whether the fix is right.

 - Experience finding systemic vulnerability patterns and driving architectural fixes with engineering teams, not only reporting individual findings.

 - Strong relationship skills with developers and stakeholders. You make security digestible, you're comfortable pushing back kindly, and people trust you.

 - Hands-on experimentation with AI in your security work, ideally building automation rather than one-off use. Experience securing AI features in a product is a strong asset.

Jobber has AI in production, but not yet at its full potential.

 - Piece together context across workflows

 - Decide what to do next

The platform doesn’t proactively help them run their business. That’s the gap.

 - Evaluation (offline + online)

 - Observability and failure handling

 - Guardrails and safety in real systems

 - Tradeoffs between autonomy vs. control

You don’t need to code daily, but you must be able to reason at the system level.

 - You have opinions about evaluation, reliability, and safety


EXECUTION

You can move fast without breaking everything.

 - You know when to iterate and when to redesign




WHY JOBBER · WHY NOW?

This is not “AI theatre.”

We already have:

What we don’t have yet is: A unified, intelligent system across the product.

Then Jobber might be the place for you! We're looking for a Principal Software Engineer, AI, to join the Office of the CEO.

The team:

This is a startup inside Jobber. A small, senior team in the Office of the CEO with a mandate to reinvent how a 1,000-person company operates in the AI era, and the backing to actually do it. Reporting to the VP of Customer Experience Innovation, the Principal Software Engineer will be the founding technical seat: you'll architect and build new AI systems from zero to production, and own the hard problems that come with putting AI at the center of how a company runs — trust, permissions, security, and quality at scale.

This is a builder's role with unusual range. One week you're designing the architecture of a system nobody at Jobber has built before; the next you're embedded with a team, shipping working AI into their real workflow and making them the hero. You'll make fast build-vs-buy calls, run POCs and kill them without sentiment, and set the technical standards that everything AI at Jobber gets held to. We're looking for someone who has shipped production AI or data systems, defaults to pragmatic technology choices, and wants founding-engineer ownership with a real company's resources behind it.

 - Drive build-vs-buy evaluations and fast POCs, with the judgment to commit hard and kill fast.

 - A track record of building production systems at Staff+ scope: data infrastructure, retrieval, or applied AI used daily by hundreds to thousands of people who depend on it.

 - Hands-on depth with the modern AI stack, and at least one battle scar from a system that showed you how confidently AI can be wrong.

 - A daily working relationship with AI tools and agents, as instruments you build with and build for.

THE ROLE:

Jobber's website is one of our most important growth engines — the place where small home-service businesses first meet the product and decide to start a trial. The Web team builds and continuously improves getjobber.com http://getjobber.com, shipping new pages, running a high-velocity experimentation program, and pushing the limits of what a marketing site can do for conversion, SEO, and AI-driven discovery.

We're looking for a Senior Front-End Developer with deep web experimentation experience — to drive high-velocity A/B and multivariate testing across our web properties while elevating our technical architecture. You'll work across our modern Jamstack stack (Next.js, Sanity headless CMS, React, TypeScript) as well as our traditional headful WordPress platform (PHP, Twig templates), expanding our component libraries and engineering high-performance CRO frameworks. CMS familiarity is essential: you'll build and optimize features across both modern headless APIs and legacy PHP/Twig codebases. This is a senior individual-contributor role with real technical influence: you'll set experimentation standards, mentor developers, and partner with the Engineering Manager on quality and site performance.

Just as importantly, we want someone who treats AI-assisted development as a core engineering skill. We're actively reshaping how we build — using AI coding agents, MCP-connected tooling, and automated workflows to move faster without sacrificing quality — and we want this person to help lead that evolution, not just keep up with it.




WHAT YOU'LL DO:

Build on a modern front-end stack

 - Engineer across a hybrid web stack — ship production features in Next.js, Sanity, and React with TypeScript, alongside ongoing support and enhancements for our headful WordPress (PHP/Twig) environment across getjobber.com http://getjobber.com.

 - Contribute to and extend our shared component library and design system so the team builds faster on consistent, reusable, well-tested foundations.

 - Own performance and accessibility as first-class requirements — Core Web Vitals, semantic and accessible markup, and fast, resilient page loads that directly support conversion.

 - Work seamlessly between headless and traditional CMS architectures — integrate APIs and structured content in Sanity while maintaining Twig-templated components in WordPress as we transition our web ecosystem.

 - Write well-tested, scalable, well-organized code and drive consistent engineering practices through code review.

 - Collaborate with our other developers on best technical practices and project decisions.

Push our AI-assisted workflow forward

 - Use AI coding tools and agents fluently (e.g. Claude, AI-assisted IDEs, agentic workflows) to accelerate development while keeping a critical eye on output quality and reliability.

 - Improve how the team works with AI — building and refining MCP integrations, prompts, and context so our tickets, content, and codebase are AI-ready.

 - Help define and benchmark team standards for AI-assisted development — identifying what works, documenting it, and raising the whole team's baseline.

Power experimentation and growth

 - Architect and execute complex A/B and multivariate experiments across high-converting marketing flows, partnering with CRO leads and data analysts to design statistically sound, performant test variants.

 - Build for experimentation velocity and statistical integrity — minimize flicker, ensure client/server-side rendering accuracy, and reduce time-to-market from test hypothesis to live variant.

 - Support SEO, LLM, and AI-search initiatives with the technical foundations (structured data, performance, rendering) that keep the site discoverable as search evolves.

Raise the technical bar

 - Set patterns and technical direction for how we build, and bring the team along through pragmatic, well-reasoned decisions.

 - Mentor and coach other front-end developers, lifting their skills and holding the team to its engineering principles.

 - Partner with the Engineering Manager on technical standards, code quality, and architecture

 - Identify and act on opportunities to improve the stack, tooling, and processes, and maintain strong team documentation.




TO BE SUCCESSFUL, YOU SHOULD HAVE:

 - Deep front-end expertise. Expert command of HTML, CSS, JavaScript/TypeScript, accessibility, and web performance, plus several years building production applications.

 - Proven web experimentation & CRO expertise. Hands-on experience architecting and shipping complex A/B, Multivariate Testing, and personalized web experiments with measurable conversion outcomes.

 - Experience with web experimentation and feature flag platforms (e.g. Kameleoon, Optimizely, VWO, LaunchDarkly) and product analytics tools (e.g. Amplitude, GA4).

 - Strong Jamstack and modern front-end stack. Mastery of Next.js, React, TypeScript, and modern rendering strategies with a focus on performance and accessibility.

 - Experience working within a design system or maintaining a shared component library.

 - Versatile CMS background (Headless Sanity & WordPress/Twig). Experience modeling content in headless CMS platforms (Sanity/Contentful) alongside hands-on proficiency in traditional WordPress, PHP, and Twig templates.

 - Hands-on AI-assisted development. You actively use AI coding tools in your day-to-day work and have a point of view on where they help, where they don't, and how to use them responsibly.

 - A growth and experimentation mindset. You're comfortable building for measurement and iteration, and you care about the business outcome your code drives.

 - Technical leadership without ego. You set standards and mentor others while staying collaborative and open to better ideas.

 - Strong communication. You collaborate easily with both technical and non-technical partners — designers, marketers, and CRO.

 - Ambitious and humble. You don't accept the status quo simply because "it's what we've always done" — you push for better, newer, more innovative approaches while staying grounded.

 - Comfort in the grey areas. You're adaptable, can prioritize amid ambiguity and changing priorities, and break large, complex problems into shippable pieces.

Nice to have:

 - Back-end familiarity. Comfort working beyond the front end: integrating APIs and services, or background experience with full-stack development.

 - Experience collaborating closely with designers in Figma.

We're looking for a Senior Product Manager, Automations Platform to be part of our AI Workflows product organization.



The team:

The Automations Platform team builds the system that lets Jobber Teammate, our AI teammate for home service businesses, do a service provider's work for them. Every automation in Jobber runs on what this team builds.



The role:

You'll make it possible for Jobber Teammate to automate every task in Jobber.

Today a handful of automations exist and each one is expensive to build. The ambition is that every task a service provider repeats in their week has an automation that does it for them. Getting there takes two things at once, and this role does both.

You'll build the platform: the authoring, execution and evaluation models that let any product team at Jobber ship an automation without first becoming AI specialists. Skill files, tool calls, and evals that make an automation measurably better over time.

You'll also build on the platform: choosing the automations that matter most, shipping them yourself, and making them easy to find, enable and trust. Being the platform's hardest customer is what keeps it honest.

Over time you'll open it up, so service providers create their own and the best ones spread to businesses like theirs.

This suits someone equally at home in an architecture discussion and a customer interview.



As Senior Product Manager you will:

 - Build a deep understanding of home service businesses and the repeated work that consumes their week.

 - Own the automation platform: how automations are authored, how they execute, and how they're evaluated and improved.

 - Make it fast and cheap for any Jobber team to ship an automation, and measure yourself on their throughput rather than your own.

 - Build the highest-impact automations yourself, and make them easy for service providers to find, enable and trust.

 - Build an Evals platform, that makes it easy to iterate on and improve automations so the quality bar is constantly raising

 - Bring the product requirements to our AI Foundations engineering team, who build the underlying agent infrastructure.

 - Define the metrics that tell you the platform works: cost and speed of building an automation, engagement with the ones we ship, and growth of the library.



To be successful, you should have:

 - 5+ years of product management experience, with evidence of shipping real AI products and seeing them through to long-term outcomes.

 - A growth mindset and someone who thrives in change and ambiguity. The AI Org you’ll join is a fast moving space and we expect that the technology, positioning, scope and roles will all continue to evolve as we learn together

 - Experience building an AI platform was genuinely adopted - won through advocacy, tooling, and documentation.

 - Experience shipping LLM-backed or ML-backed products, with real respect for how they fail.

 - A track record of making a contested technical decision and making it stick.

 - Comfort thinking in unit economics, because the cost of building an automation decides whether this strategy is real.



Bonus points if you have:

 - Experience with agent frameworks, tool calling, or evaluation and observability systems for AI.

 - Experience with workflow automation, or no-code and low-code builder products.

 - Experience in home services, field service, or SMB software.

We’re looking for a Senior Product Manager, Supply to be part of our Ecosystem product organization.

The team:

Materials are one of the largest costs in a home service business. We're helping home service businesses manage this side of their work, connecting the supply chain directly into Jobber so service pros can find, price, and manage materials as part of their everyday workflows.

The role:

We're looking for a Senior Product Manager who is excited to connect a whole new part of the ecosystem into Jobber, solving problems for service providers at every step of their workflow. From the plumber who needs to know a quote will actually be profitable, to the contractor who needs parts to show up on time to keep a job on track..

In this role, you’ll own the strategy and execution behind Jobber Supply. You’ll work across a genuinely broad product surface: supplier catalog integrations, real-time and account-specific pricing, materials and cost management, and purchase orders. You’ll be doing it while sitting alongside Business Development in live supplier partnership cycles, technical evaluations, and roadmap conversations with some of the largest supply partners in North America.

You'll identify where material workflows break down for service pros today, where the gap between what a job was quoted at and what it actually cost erodes their margins, and where the biggest opportunities are to make Jobber the obvious place where materials and everyday workflows come together to make their business more profitable.

This role is a strong fit for someone who is deeply customer-curious, commercially sharp, and comfortable operating in zero-to-one territory. Someone who can lead supplier partnership conversations, build internal influence, work through data models with engineers, and see how everything flows across the end-to-end workflow without losing the thread. You should be excited to own outcomes for service professionals and Jobber.


As Senior Product Manager you will:

 - Build a deep understanding of our customers: home service businesses (such as plumbing companies, landscapers, electricians etc.) and how they source, price, order, and track the materials that power their jobs.

 - Drive complex, business-critical Supply product initiatives. Define a vision, strategy, and roadmap that spans supplier catalogs, materials management, and job costing.

 - Prioritize opportunities into a cohesive product roadmap that ties customer needs and supplier partners with Jobber’s business goals and competitive landscape.

 - Synthesize learnings across the material ecosystem into common denominator product investments,

 - Balance short-term wins with long-term strategic bets that span across workflows.

Small business owners don't just need software - they need a financial partner.

Running a home service business means juggling cash flow, fronting the cost of materials, protecting the business from risk, and helping customers afford bigger jobs. Today, most small business owners stitch this together with personal credit cards, generic bank accounts, insurance brokers who don't understand their trade, and financing options their customers can't access at the moment they need them. It's fragmented, it's expensive, and none of it is built for how they actually work.

That's the opportunity for Fintech New Bets.

We're looking for a Staff Product Manager, Fintech New Bets to discover, validate, and launch Jobber's next generation of financial products - in areas like insurance, consumer financing, and spend and money management (think a card offering and business banking built for Pros). This is a high-impact, highly senior individual contributor role at the intersection of zero-to-one product building and deep fintech domain expertise. You'll take loosely defined opportunities and turn them into live products with real customers and real revenue.

The team

Fintech is one of the fastest-growing parts of Jobber, and a core strategic priority for us as a company. We're investing in this growing area because we believe embedding financial tools within our product deepens our ability to help small businesses be successful.

Whether it's helping small businesses get paid using Jobber Payments, getting access to capital to invest in growth, or offering financing to our customers' customers, we believe small business owners should have seamless access to financial tools that allow them to thrive.

New Bets is the team charged with finding what comes next. As Jobber's fintech business scales beyond payments, we're expanding into new, high-impact financial products - and this role is the product leadership engine of that expansion. You'll work in close partnership with your commercial and strategy counterparts on the New Bets team, who own business cases, partner negotiations, and unit economics - together, you'll take new bets from idea, to business case, to shipped product.

Simply put, we care much more about our customers than any financial institution ever will. That's our superpower.

The role

We're looking for a Staff Product Manager, Fintech New Bets who brings deep product expertise, strong zero-to-one instincts, and the ability to lead through influence across a complex, ambiguous, and high-stakes domain.

In this role, you'll own the product side of Jobber's newest fintech bets. You'll look across the financial life of a home service business - how they spend, borrow, insure, and bank - and identify which products Jobber should build, buy, or partner to deliver. You'll run rapid discovery and validation, shape build-vs-partner decisions with embedded finance and banking-as-a-service providers, and lead the first versions of these products from pilot through to scale.

Unlike our established product areas, there is no playbook here. You'll be expected to operate with high autonomy, form conviction from thin data, kill ideas that don't clear the bar, and bring cross-functional partners along with clarity and speed. This is a role for someone who is energized by ambiguity, moves fast without breaking trust, and has shipped financial products before.

As a Staff Product Manager, Fintech New Bets you will:

 - Take new bets from zero to one: frame the customer problem, size the opportunity, design and run lean validation experiments and pilots, and make evidence-based go/no-go recommendations.

 - Lead build-vs-buy-vs-partner decisions, evaluating embedded finance, banking-as-a-service, insurance, and lending partners on capabilities, economics, risk, and customer experience - and shaping those partnerships alongside our commercial team.

 - Ship and scale first versions of new financial products, defining the MVP, sequencing the roadmap, and iterating quickly based on customer and market feedback.

 - Partner deeply with Design, Engineering, Data, Risk, Compliance, Legal, Finance, and GTM to navigate the regulatory and operational realities of launching financial products.

 - Use qualitative and quantitative insights - including unit economics, adoption signals, and risk performance - to form deep conviction about which bets deserve further investment.

 - Elevate product thinking across the fintech group, shaping how other PMs and leaders evaluate new opportunities, frame trade-offs, and make decisions in emerging financial domains.

 - Balance the urgency of proving new bets quickly with the rigor required to build durable, trustworthy financial products at scale.

To be successful, you should have:

 - Extensive product management experience, with a proven track record of taking new products from concept to launch - ideally including at least one financial product with meaningful revenue accountability.

 - Experience operating at a staff or principal level - defining strategy across ambiguous problem spaces, influencing without authority, and shaping org-wide product direction.

 - Deep familiarity with fintech products such as card issuing, spend management, business banking, insurance, or lending - and an understanding of the partner, risk, and compliance ecosystems behind them.

 - Exceptional product sense and commercial rigor. You can pressure-test unit economics and business cases as comfortably as you can critique a customer flow.

 - A bias for validated learning: you know how to de-risk a bet cheaply, when to double down, and when to walk away.

 - The ability to connect deep customer insight to long-term business strategy and communicate it clearly to senior stakeholders, external partners, and cross-functional teams.

 - A high bar for quality, ownership, and outcomes - combined with the judgment to know when to go deep and when to zoom out.

Bonus points if you have:

 - Experience launching embedded fintech products in a vertical SaaS or platform business

 - Experience working with banking-as-a-service or embedded finance providers, card networks, sponsor banks, insurance carriers or MGAs, or consumer lending partners.

 - Experience serving small businesses, particularly in home and field services.

We also own the modernization of our frontend stack, keeping it aligned with industry standards and emerging technologies to enhance developer efficiency and user experience. Joining this team is an opportunity to work on cutting-edge web technologies and help shape the future of Jobber’s online experience!

The role of Staff Software Engineer at Jobber:

As a technical champion and force multiplier, you lead and mentor teams of exceptional engineers while collaborating closely with Product and Design partners to tackle complex technical challenges. Your expertise spans architecture, design, and hands-on coding, allowing you to have a significant impact on the product and our customers. A portion of your time is allocated to "Staff Dev Projects," which may include cross-team initiatives, work acceleration within your team, exploration of emerging technologies, addressing technical debt, or investing in the future of engineering at Jobber. In addition, you customize, extend and experiment with tools, models, harnesses and processes to increase the effectiveness of yourself, your team and mentor others to do the same.

As a Staff Software Engineer, you will:

 - Collaborate closely with cross-functional teams to conceptualize, design, and iteratively deliver high-impact features that address customer needs

 - Partner with Product and Design teams to shape and define the strategic product roadmap

 - Identify and lead large-scale initiatives that drive innovation across multiple teams or departments

 - Actively participate in code reviews and testing processes to ensure code quality and maintainability

 - Champion the development of consistent engineering practices and reusable code solutions to enhance overall efficiency

 - Lead and facilitate group discussions to drive consensus on optimal solutions for complex customer problems

 - Research, promote, and implement industry best practices within your team's domain, staying at the forefront of technological advancements

 - Effectively communicate complex technical concepts to diverse audiences, bridging the gap between technical and non-technical stakeholders

 - Provide mentorship and guidance to team members at all levels, fostering their professional growth and career development

 - Build with AI as a core part of how you work. We expect engineers to delegate real work to agents daily, verify what comes back, and keep improving their own setup so each task makes the next one easier.

To be successful, you should have:

 - Demonstrated expertise in developing highly scalable, robust software solutions across multiple layers of the technology stack

 - Daily hands-on experience building with agentic AI tools, beyond autocomplete or chat: you delegate real work to agents as part of how you ship.

 - Demonstrated expertise in developing highly scalable, robust software solutions across multiple layers of the technology stack

 - Proven leadership experience in guiding teams through complex, high-impact projects and serving as a technical lead

 - Exceptional proficiency in software design, architecture, and coding, with a focus on maintainability and performance

 - Outstanding collaboration and communication skills, coupled with the ability to significantly amplify the team’s productivity and effectiveness through mentorship/coaching

 - Strong self-motivation and resourcefulness, with the capacity to independently identify and leverage necessary resources for project delivery and problem-solving

 - Ability to navigate ambiguity and prioritize tasks effectively in dynamic, fast-paced environments

 - Passionate commitment to continuous learning and professional growth, with a track record of staying current with emerging technologies and industry trends

It would be really great if you had:

 - Experience with our development stack: React, React Native, TypeScript, GraphQL API layer, and Ruby on Rails on AWS. 

 - Led cross-team initiatives and projects

Hiring Process and Team Match-Making:

Using our engineering hiring process, we will explore the skills and qualifications you bring and match you with one of the teams currently hiring. Our hiring process has an interview with a Talent team member (45mins), a Hiring Manager Interview (60mins), a take-home challenge with a follow-up Functional Interview (90mins) and a Senior Leadership Interview (45mins). If a team in particular excites you, feel free to mention it to your Talent Partner! 

Location:

We believe great collaboration is intentional, and sometimes that means coming together in person to build, brainstorm, and connect. To support this, the role is open to candidates based in one of our hub cities: Edmonton, Toronto, Vancouver, or Kitchener-Waterloo.

Compensation:

At Jobber, we believe that compensation should be transparent, fair, and supportive of your experience and growth. This role has a minimum annual salary of $169,200, a midpoint of $199,100, and a maximum salary of $228,900, designed to reflect the progression from learning the ropes to truly excelling. 

We design our compensation to reflect each new hire's skills, experience, and the complexity of the role, ensuring a fair and competitive salary. Our range is intentionally broad to support growth and long-term impact, with fully established hires typically starting around the midpoint. The higher end of the range is reserved for those who have demonstrated deep expertise and lasting contributions, while offers below the midpoint reflect strong potential with room to develop. This approach ensures that compensation aligns with both an individual's current capabilities and their opportunity for future growth.

Base salary is just one part of a total compensation package that will include equity rewards, annual stipends for health and wellness, retirement savings matching, and an extended health package with fully paid premiums for body and mind. Your professional growth matters to us too! You'll have access to a dedicated talent development program that includes career coaching and opportunities for career development.

 We believe in transparency and open conversations about compensation. If you have any questions about our approach, we're happy to discuss them throughout the hiring process!

What you can expect from Jobber:

 - A total compensation package that includes an extended health benefits package with fully paid premiums for both body and mind, matching in RRSP, TFSA or FHSA, and stock options.

 - A dedicated Talent Development team and access to coaching, learning, and leadership programs to help you grow your career, reach your goals, and unlock your full potential.

 - A unique opportunity to build, grow, and leave your impact on a $400-billion industry that has no dominant player...yet.

 - To work with a group of people who are humble, supportive, and give a sh*t about our customers.

We believe that diverse teams perform better and that fostering an inclusive work environment is a key part of growing a successful team. We welcome people of diverse backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives. We are an equal opportunity employer, and we are committed to working with applicants requesting accommodation at any stage of the hiring process.



A bit more about us:

Job by job, we’re transforming the way service is delivered. Your lawn care provider, home cleaning service, plumber or painter could use Jobber to better connect with their customers, save time in the office, invoice faster, and get paid! We’re bringing tens of thousands of people together with technology to deliver billions of dollars a year in services to happy customers. Jobber exists to help make these small businesses successful, and when they’re successful we all win!

ABOUT YOUR ROLE

As the Director, Engineering you will lead the vision and execution for the foundational systems that power our entire engineering organization. Your mandate spans four critical pillars: architecting the modularization of our core Python/FastAPI monolith, accelerating our transition to an AI-native engineering culture, empowering product teams with tools to build AI-enabled features, and establishing a robust Application Security (AppSec) posture.



You will manage a group of engineering managers and staff engineers. You will act as a strategic multiplier for the company, treating our internal platform as a top-tier product. Your ultimate goal is to create secure, high-velocity "paved paths" that make our product teams incredibly fast, while systematically reducing technical debt and security risks.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Direct the Monolith Evolution: Own the multi-year technical strategy to safely decouple our legacy Python/Jinja monolith into a modern, modular FastAPI architecture using Domain-Driven Design and zero-downtime database migration tactics.

 - Drive the AI-Native SDLC: Champion the rollout and adoption of AI-assisted coding tools and AI-augmented workflows across the entire engineering organization, systematically measuring and improving developer productivity.

 - Enable AI Feature Development: Treat the internal platform as a product. Guide the development of intuitive SDKs, data pipelines, and internal tools that reduce cognitive load and allow product engineers to easily integrate LLMs and build AI-powered features.

 - Lead Application Security (AppSec): Champion a "shift-left" security culture. Embed secure coding practices, automated vulnerability scanning, and threat modeling directly into developer workflows, ensuring our core platform is resilient against modern threats.

 - Oversee Core Shared Services: Drive the scale, security, and reliability of enterprise-critical systems, including Identity (AuthN/AuthZ, OAuth2, RBAC), Audit Logs, and high-throughput API & MCP Gateways.

 - Navigate Org-Wide Boundaries: Negotiate complex refactoring timelines with Product leaders and collaborate seamlessly with other Engineering teams and DevOps to align our platform capabilities with infrastructure.

 - Build a World-Class Organization: Recruit, mentor, and grow a high-performing organization of engineering managers and staff/principal engineers, fostering a culture of architectural pragmatism and deep developer empathy.




QUALIFICATIONS

 - 15+ years of software engineering experience, with at least 5+ years in engineering leadership, including explicitly managing managers and leading multiple teams.

 - High AI Fluency: Proven experience architecting systems that support AI features (LLMs, RAG, tool calling) and a track record of driving AI-assisted development tools (AI SDLC) across engineering teams.

 - An executive track record of successfully guiding massive monolith-to-modular migrations and decoupling shared database schemas in high-traffic, business-critical environments.

 - Deep strategic understanding of Application Security principles, Identity/Access Management (OAuth 2.0, OIDC), and modern API traffic management.

 - Strong technical fluency in Python and FastAPI ecosystems, with the ability to guide Staff-level engineers through complex architectural decisions involving both modern APIs and legacy applications.

 - Exceptional executive communication skills, with the ability to translate complex technical, security, and AI trade-offs into business value.




COMPENSATION

Compensation for this position includes a base salary, bonus, equity and a variety of benefits. The U.S. base salary range is $230,000 - $285,000. Actual base salaries will be based on candidate-specific factors, including experience, skillset, and location, and local minimum pay requirements as applicable.

Benefits include:

 - Health, dental, and vision care for you and your family

 - Life insurance

 - Mental wellness coverage

 - Fertility and growing family support

 - Flex Time Off in addition to company-paid holidays

 - Paid family leave, medical leave, and bereavement leave policies

 - Retirement saving plans

 - Allowance to customize your work and technology setup at home

 - Annual professional development stipend

ABOUT YOUR ROLE

As a Senior Software Engineer at Juniper Square, you're a hands-on individual contributor who designs, builds, and operates production systems powering core workflows for institutional financial clients. You bring deep technical expertise to your team, drive complex projects independently, and collaborate closely with Staff engineers, product, design, and QA to ship reliable, well-designed systems.

We're hiring Senior Software Engineers across two teams:

 - Accounting: Join the team that owns Juniper Square's core accounting data and workflows (the bedrock that other product areas build on). You'll work on the transactions platform, expand third-party integrations, build out custom financial and general ledger reporting, and help build a proprietary waterfall model from the ground up, as the platform evolves from a reporting engine into a full accounting engine.

 - Treasury: Join the team building Juniper Square's Treasury platform, the system that brings transactions, balances, and bank data into and across the platform. You'll work on expanding bank integrations, a visualization and reporting layer for payments and treasury data, and vendor exports that connect treasury data to accounting, on a team that has already processed $500M+ in transactions.



WHAT YOU'LL DO

Build & Operate Production Systems

 - Design, build, and ship production-quality systems, APIs, and services - from foundational platform capabilities to customer-facing product experiences

 - Own projects end-to-end: translating requirements into technical designs, implementation, testing, deployment, and ongoing iteration

 - Partner with product, design, and engineering to translate requirements into well-designed technical solutions

 - Contribute to the team's evolving practices around AI-accelerated development, testing, and code review

Collaborate Cross-Functionally

 - Work closely with product, design, QA, and cross-functional partners to meet timelines and align solutions to business goals

 - Provide clear, accessible technical context to both technical and non-technical stakeholders

Domain Expertise

 - Grow into a subject-matter expert in your domain (Accounting, Treasury, or Platform), with a deep understanding of the data, workflows, and customer needs specific to that space




QUALIFICATIONS

Required

 - Experience with relational/NoSQL databases, including schema design, query optimization, and data modeling

ABOUT YOUR ROLE

We are seeking a Senior Staff Software Engineer to lead the architecture and evolution of the core systems that power Juniper Square — the distributed services, cloud infrastructure, and developer platform on which every product, workflow, and AI capability is built. You will define the vision, architecture, operating model, and execution roadmap required to evolve from team-by-team infrastructure decisions to a cohesive, paved-road platform that enables every engineering team to ship reliable, secure, and performant software at speed.

This role anchors a strategic priority for our GPX line of business: taking Juniper Square upmarket to serve the largest private equity institutions in the world — firms managing $100B+ in AUM. Serving these PE titans demands a step-change in everything our systems do: order of magnitude increase in data and traffic volumes; enterprise-grade security, and integration expectations. You will architect the systems foundation that makes this scalable.

This is a deeply hands-on leadership role for a technical expert who leads by building: you will actively design systems, prototype solutions, write and review code, and guide teams through their most complex technical challenges.

Your mandate spans the full systems estate. You will modernize our service architecture and cloud foundation, define architecture across compute, networking, service communication, multi-tenancy, and observability, and build the systems substrate — including the infrastructure powering JunieAI and agentic workloads — on which teams across the business build and operate software. Throughout, you will hold our production systems to the availability, latency, security, and cost standards expected of a platform administering $300B+ in private markets assets.

You will work closely with engineering leadership, product teams, security, and executive stakeholders to align technology strategy with business outcomes, mentor engineers, and build a culture of operational excellence. Success in this role means not only delivering a modern systems platform but also elevating the team's capabilities, processes, and ways of working to operate as a true platform engineering organization.
While this is a remote role, some travel is required — to in-person leadership meetups, team offsites, and to customer sites in support of enterprise engagements where deep technical presence matters.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

Architecture & Technical Leadership

 - Define and own the end-to-end systems architecture strategy across services, infrastructure, and developer platform

 - Designing frameworks and design patterns that accelerate the work of the rest of engineering org

 - Design scalable, fault-tolerant distributed systems spanning synchronous APIs, asynchronous workflows, and event-driven architectures

 - Establish standards for service design, API contracts, multi-tenancy, and inter-service communication

 - Lead architecture reviews and technical decision-making for high-stakes, cross-cutting initiatives

 - Drive adoption of modern architectures (event-driven systems, platform engineering, infrastructure as code)

Hands-On Engineering

 - Design and prototype critical platform and infrastructure components

 - Write production-quality code for complex or high-impact areas

 - Review service designs, infrastructure changes, and performance-critical code paths

 - Troubleshoot performance, scalability, and reliability issues across services, queues, caches, and databases

 - Optimize workloads for latency, throughput, concurrency, and cost

Platform & Infrastructure Ownership

 - Design and architect a scalable cloud platform supporting compute, networking, storage, service orchestration, and deployment across all product lines

 - Build a paved-road developer platform — golden paths, internal tooling, CI/CD, and self-service infrastructure — that makes the right way the easy way

 - Create reusable platform primitives and internal APIs that product teams can compose rather than rebuild

 - Enable self-service infrastructure for engineering teams through standardized patterns, templates, and platform capabilities

 - Partner with AI workflow teams, product, and security teams to support production AI workloads, from inference pipelines to agent fleets

 - Design systems for safe agentic execution, including isolation boundaries, resource governance, auditability, and human-in-the-loop controls

 - Ensure reliability, scalability, and resilience of the platform, including high availability, monitoring, and disaster recovery readiness

Enterprise Scale & Upmarket Readiness

 - Architect core systems to handle the data volumes and structural complexity of $100B+ AUM managers: thousands of entities, tens of thousands of LPs, and deep multi-tier fund structures

 - Define scalability targets and re-architect bottlenecked systems ahead of demand, ensuring performance holds at 10x current transaction and data volumes

 - Design enterprise integration surfaces — APIs, bulk data interfaces, and ERP/GL connectivity — that fit into the existing technology estates of large institutional GPs

 - Meet the security, compliance, and operational diligence expectations of the largest PE firms, such as, SSO/SCIM, granular entitlements, audit trails, and data residency

 - Serve as the senior technical voice in enterprise sales and onboarding conversations where architecture, scale, and resiliency are decision criteria

Reliability & Operational Excellence

Our mission is to unlock the agent economy by empowering developers and enterprises with the secure, scalable foundations they need to build, deploy, adopt, and trust agentic applications. To do this, we’re building the real-time, in-band, contextual guardrails required to transition from human-driven to truly autonomous and agentic workflows that give users, builders, and security teams the confidence and control they need to bring agents out of the lab and into production.

At our core, we’re laser-focused on delivering a delightful, best-in-class developer experience that gives them the tools they need to create category-defining applications and experiences while giving platform and security teams the security, scalability, visibility, control, and enablement they need to accelerate their organizations journey to becoming agent native.

We’re a small, distributed team of repeat founders and builders, with backgrounds from Snyk https://www.snyk.io, Auth0 https://auth0.com, HashiCorp https://hashicorp.com, and Heroku https://heroku.com.

Joining Keycard now means helping define not just our technology, but also the culture and company we’re building together—during a once-in-a-generation platform shift.


THE ROLE

We're hiring a Product Manager to own how teams evaluate Keycard, and the developer experience they meet when they do.

Keycard is a control plane for agents: identity, credential exchange, delegation, policy, and audit. Every customer starts with an evaluation, and today a field engineer runs each one by hand: setup, first credential exchange, integration questions. Your job is to turn that walkthrough into product, so an evaluation can run well without us in the room.

You'll define what a successful evaluation looks like for an agent-identity product, instrument the journey so we can see where evaluators stall, then work with engineering to fix the worst spots. Sometimes the fix is a feature, more often it's a better quickstart, a template repo, an error message that says what to do next, or a docs page that assumed too much context.

Expect to spend real time with the people running evaluations: watching onboarding sessions, sitting in on field-engineering walkthroughs, reading support threads, and finding out why a team went quiet mid-eval.



WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Own the evaluation journey end to end, from first touch through first credential exchange to a production decision, including how each stage is defined and measured.

 - Set the evaluation milestones and metrics that product, engineering, and go-to-market all report against.

 - Own the developer experience an evaluation runs on: SDK quickstarts, CLI onboarding, console setup, docs, and template repos.

 - Drive time-to-first-credential-exchange down, and be the voice of developer ergonomics in engineering's API and CLI design discussions.

 - Turn what field engineering does by hand into self-guided paths: eval guides, reference architectures, in-product guidance. Run experiments and cut the ones that don't work.

 - Work with DevRel and marketing on how evaluations start, and with sales and field engineering on when a self-guided eval needs a human in the room.


WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - You've been a PM on a developer product where evaluation and adoption were your numbers (dev tools, infrastructure, API platforms, or security).

 - Technical enough to be credible with engineers. You can read an SDK quickstart and see where a developer would bounce, follow an API design discussion, and pull your own numbers in SQL or an analytics tool.

 - You have taste in developer experience. You can articulate why one CLI feels good and another doesn't, and you notice error messages, defaults, and docs structure the way a designer notices spacing.

 - You build with AI tools yourself and follow the agent ecosystem closely enough to have real opinions about it.

 - You start from instrumentation. If the data you need doesn't exist, you get it added before forming theories about where evaluations drop off.

 - Comfortable in a category with no playbook. Agent identity is new, and a lot of this job is deciding which questions are worth answering.

 - You write clearly. Much of this role's output is docs, problem statements, and experiment readouts that other people act on.

 - Experience with growth tooling: product analytics, experimentation frameworks, lifecycle messaging.

 - Docs, quickstarts, or templates you shipped that developers actually used.

 - You'd rather ship a fix this week than present a strategy deck about it next month.

 - You treat quickstarts and docs as product surfaces that deserve real design attention.

 - You want to define the evaluation motion for a new category from scratch.

 - You like being early: small team, direct access to founders and customers, no layers between you and what ships.


WHAT WE OFFER

 - Build at the Frontier: Work every day at the frontier of agent-native systems — shipping, inventing, and iterating on technology that hasn’t been built before. You’ll be given huge autonomy, the opportunity to gain mastery, and the chance to work in a team that holds each other accountable to succeed.

 - Truly Agent-Native Culture: At Keycard, we don’t just enable others to adopt agents — we use them ourselves to build. You’ll help shape an organization that embeds AI into its foundation as an enduring competitive advantage.

 - Compensation With Upside: Market-competitive salaries and generous equity packages (4-year vest, 1-year cliff) give you the security to focus on building — and the asymmetric upside of ownership in a company chasing a category-defining mission.

 - Comprehensive Benefits & Recharge: Health, dental, vision, and paramedical coverage for you and your family, plus 4 weeks vacation, 11 statutory holidays, and 1 volunteer day annually. We encourage at least 2 weeks off each year to fully recharge.

 - Tools That Keep You Ahead: A new MacBook Pro, a $500 stipend for peripherals, and the best AI tools available so you can work at the forefront of agent-native workflows.

 - Remote-First Flexibility: We are a remote-first team prioritizing asynchronous collaboration, with hiring focused in North and South America. Work where you’re strongest — we just want the best.

Keycard is building the fundamental unlock for the next generation of software: enabling truly secure and trusted agentic applications. Engineering Lead: Options



About Keyrock



Since our beginnings in 2017, we've grown to be a leading change-maker in the digital asset space, renowned for our partnerships and innovation.



Today, we rock with over 200 team members around the world. Our diverse team hails from 42 nationalities, with backgrounds ranging from DeFi natives to PhDs. Predominantly remote, we have hubs in London, Madrid, Brussels, Singapore , New York and Paris, and host regular online and offline hangouts to keep the crew tight.



We are trading on more than 80 exchanges, and working with a wide array of asset issuers. As a well-established market maker, our distinctive expertise led us to expand rapidly. Today, our services span market making, options trading, high-frequency trading, OTC, and DeFi trading desks as well as asset and wealth management. Keyrock is looking to expand and establish itself as a full-service capital markets and asset & wealth management financial institution through both organic innovation and inorganic growth.



But we’re more than a service provider. We’re an initiator. We have been pioneers in adopting the Rust Development language for our algorithmic trading systems, and champions of its use in the industry. We upgrade Web3 ecosystems by injecting liquidity into promising DeFi, RWA, and NFT protocols. And we push the industry's progress with our research and governance initiatives.



At Keyrock, we're not just envisioning the future of digital assets. We're actively building it.





Mission statement
We are looking for a Head of Engineering / Engineering Lead with strong experience in systematic options trading to lead our Options Engineering team.

In this role, you will be responsible for leading the Options Engineering team, driving continuous improvement across the trading infrastructure, and supporting the evolution of our systematic options trading platform. This includes areas such as automated quoting, execution, risk controls, pricing workflows, and production reliability.

We are primarily looking for candidates based in European time zones or the US East Coast time zone.

We are looking for someone who can:

 - Lead and grow an Options Engineering team of around 7 engineers

 - Bring hands-on experience in systematic options trading, ideally including options market-making, automated quoting, execution, and risk management

 - Own and evolve an existing Rust-native systematic options trading platform

 - Provide strong technical direction across trading infrastructure, system design, performance, reliability, and risk controls

 - Work pragmatically through complex engineering and trading-system challenges

 - Partner closely with trading, quant, product, risk, and infrastructure stakeholders

 - Balance technical leadership with people leadership, delivery ownership, and operational discipline



Required Experience

 - 7+ years of experience in systematic trading, options market-making or low-latency trading systems

 - Strong hands-on experience with Rust, C++, or C

 - Willingness to become deeply proficient in Rust, if not already

 - Strong understanding of algorithmic options trading, including automated quoting, execution, pricing, risk controls, and market data workflows

 - Experience building or maintaining low-latency trading systems, ideally within options or derivatives markets

 - Experience working with SQL databases in production environments, with PostgreSQL preferred

 - Familiarity with functional testing, component testing, and production-grade validation practices

 - Strong understanding of distributed systems, service boundaries, and production reliability

 - Strong knowledge of gRPC and experience working with Node.js-based services is preferred

 - Previous experience with crypto exchange connectivity and/or FPGA technologies is strongly preferred



Leadership & Working Style

 - Strong team player with the ability to lead, mentor, and guide engineers

 - Pragmatic approach to problem-solving, system design, and implementation

 - Able to balance latency, reliability, safety, complexity, and delivery speed

 - Comfortable making technical decisions under uncertainty

 - Demonstrates outside-the-box thinking while staying grounded in practical delivery

 - Communicates clearly and effectively, especially in unfamiliar or ambiguous contexts where clarity is critical

 - Able to work closely with traders, quants, risk, product, and infrastructure stakeholders

 - Strong ownership mindset, especially for production trading systems
 



Our recruitment philosophy



We value self-awareness and powerful communication skills in our recruitment process. We seek fiercely passionate people who understand themselves and their career goals. We're after those with the right skills and a conscious choice to join our field. The perfect fit? A crypto enthusiast who’s driven, collaborative, acts with ownership and delivers solid, scalable outcomes.





Our offer

 - A competitive salary package

 - Autonomy in your time management thanks to flexible working hours and the opportunity to work remotely

 - The freedom to create your own entrepreneurial experience by being part of a team of people in search of excellence





As an employer we are committed to building a positive and collaborative work environment. We welcome employees of all backgrounds, and hire, reward and promote entirely based on merit and performance.



Due to the nature of our business and external requirements, we perform background checks on all potential employees, passing which is a prerequisite to join Keyrock.
